location: Exhibit 11 box 'One answer, never investment advice'
claim: Copilot’s standing instructions (its system prompt) are tested so it will “never provide investment advice”
earlier_receipt: https://www.zenml.io/llmops-database/agentic-ai-architecture-for-investment-management-platform (fetched 2026-10-20): "For every intended behavior encoded in system prompts, they generate comprehensive test cases." / "For example, if a system prompt states “you must never provide investment advice,” they work with subject matter experts to:". I could not get the YouTube captions: the track list loaded but the English caption file came back empty. So the speaker's exact words are from our local transcript, /home/user/ai_game/blackrock-aladdin/04-transcripts/timestamped/yt_oyqeCHFM5U4.m4a.ts.txt:116-121: "[10:25] ... So for example if I write you're a lot in copilot / [10:30] You must never provide investment advice. What is investment advice? ... [10:44] And again, this is a very dummy example, but we do this for every system problem / [10:48] We do this for every intended behavior we code into our system prompts"
earlier_finding: The testing practice and the quoted words are accurate. The example is about Copilot: "you're a lot in copilot" is the machine transcription of "You're Aladdin Copilot". But the speaker presents the rule as a hypothetical ("for example if I write", "a very dummy example"). ZenML's summary also frames it as an example ("if a system prompt states"). Neither source says Copilot's actual system prompt contains this rule. Suggested rewording: "the team tests every behaviour written into Copilot's system prompts; the talk's example is a rule that it must 'never provide investment advice' 8". Web search was unavailable because this turn's search budget was used up, so I found no further independent source.
